title: Goodbye, ‘China Plus One’: The Real Change in US China Policy
gist: Donald Trump personally greeted Xi Jinping at Joint Base Andrews on September 23, 2026 and hosted a lavish state visit in Washington, drawing bipartisan criticism that the pageantry rewards a rival. The author argues the ceremony is only the surface and that the US-China relationship has begun to take a new direction beneath it.

insights.claim: Donald Trump greeted Xi Jinping in person at Joint Base Andrews on the evening of September 23, 2026 at the start of Xi's state visit, a rare gesture for an American president, followed by a state dinner, cannon salute and the gift of a bald eagle sculpture.
insights.so_what: Exceptional protocol signals Trump's personal investment in a deal-oriented relationship with Xi, a positive signal for near-term US-China trade stability.
insights.quote: greeted him in person at Joint Base Andrews on the evening of September 23, a rare gesture for an American president

insights.claim: Critics in both US parties warned that the pageantry of Xi's state visit would reward a rival.
insights.so_what: Congressional pushback could constrain how far a Trump-Xi rapprochement goes, e.g. on export controls or tariffs.

insights.claim: Beneath the state-visit ceremony, the US-China bilateral relationship has begun to take a new direction, according to the author.
insights.so_what: A substantive turn in US China policy could change supply-chain diversification incentives that have driven investment away from China.
